title: Intelligent eviction & routing safety net for mid-rollout variant degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We lack a unified runtime policy that (a) detects behavioral degradation for a model variant during a live canary/A-B roll, (b) atomically evicts affected in-flight sessions without user-visible corruption, and (c) re-routes traffic across region/tier gracefully while preserving SLOs and minimizing cost. Current implementations either (1) immediately roll back model versions cluster-wide (too coarse), or (2) allow degraded responses to leak into production during slow rollbacks. This ticket designs and implements an intelligent eviction + routing safety net that coordinates compatibility scoring, region-aware priority queues, and tiered capacity fallbacks tied into canary and shadow traffic pipelines.
updates: 2026-02-24: Scoping meeting with product and SRE. Agreed on three axes: semantics (compatibility), proximity (region/latency), and cost-tier (dedicated vs hosted).
2026-03-01: Prototype of compatibility scoring lambda implemented (repo: github.com/redwood/runtime/policies#compat-score-proto). Runs synthetic probes and returns score 0-100 per variant.
2026-03-04: Instrumentation hooks added to routing gateway to annotate requests with rollout metadata (canary_id, variant_score, origin_region). PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1428.

2026-03-08: Determined eviction semantics: graceful drain for long-running chats (allow KV-prefix completion for up to 5s), immediate diversion for stateless text completions. Added safety net circuit-breaker threshold at 5% degraded quantile breach.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility score evaluated every 30s and published to routing decisions; scores < 40 mark variant as degraded.
Routing gateway can atomically divert new requests away from degraded variant and progressively evict in-flight sessions according to configured policy (graceful vs immediate).
>99% of diversion decisions complete within 200ms of score update under normal load.

Auto-rollback trigger fires only after: (a) metric delta persists for 3 consecutive evaluation windows, and (b) canary traffic share >= configured minimum. Rollback executes with traffic-shift plan and post-rollback health probes.
End-to-end integration tests for region failover (simulated zone outage), tiered-capacity fallback (dedicated -> hosted), and A/B experiment reporting complete in CI.
implementation_notes: Design summary: 1) Compatibility scoring: combine semantic checks (BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics for structured outputs), latency/error spikes, and token-quality regressions measured against canary prompt set. 2) Routing decision graph: controller takes scores + region health + SLO headroom + cost budget and outputs 'serve','quarantine','evict' decisions per variant. 3) Eviction semantics: two strategies (GRACEFUL_DRAIN, IMMEDIATE_REDIRECT) set per route. 4) Fallback policy: priority list [same-region-compatible-variant, cross-region-compatible-variant (nearest), lower-cost-compatible-variant, hosted-compatible-variant]. 5) Safety fences: minimum healthy capacity must remain; if not met, circuit-breaker halts rollout and pages SRE.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive diversion reduces user exposure but can increase latency by routing cross-region.
- Semantic scoring gives earlier signal for hallucination/regression but is compute-heavy; we balance by sampling 5-10% of traffic and running full checks only on shadowed copies.
- Automatic eviction may interfere with A/B statistical power; we only apply hard evictions outside experiments or after power-preserving adjustments to hypothesis sampling.
risks:
- False positives from compatibility heuristics could cause unnecessary rollback and churn.
- Cross-region diversion may violate data residency in certain tenants (RBAC flags required).
- Eviction of in-flight stateful chats needs careful KV cache synchronization to avoid partial outputs.
mitigations:
- Add confidence windows and require multi-window confirmation before auto-rollback.
- Integrate tenant residency metadata into routing rules; respect private deployments by skipping cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed.
- For stateful sessions, implement KV-prefetch and replay buffer to allow safe handoff between variants when possible.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for score-to-decision logic. 2) Integration harness that replays real prompt traces and injects synthetic degradations. 3) Staged canary in sandbox with 5% traffic and an observability dashboard showing variant score, error rate, latency p95, and user-visible regression rate. 4) Simulated region outage test to validate failover ordering and timing.
next_steps: 1) Finish PR #1453 unit tests and load test the compatibility scorer. 2) Wire routing decision outputs into canary controller and add audit trail entries. 3) Schedule staged canary with two internal teams next week. 4) Draft postmortem template for rollback events.
notes: Related: coordinate with Legal for data residency exemptions and with Sales for customers on dedicated deployments to opt into cross-region fallback. Also discuss whether cost-tier fallbacks should be visible to customers in the Console (config toggle).
